lines: Restitution is not a word. It is what you do next.
Then settle it plainly. Pay, bargain honestly, walk away worse, or make a threat you cannot take back.
If you want this repaired, choose how you mean to repair it.
Fine. Not free, but less. Pay {payment_count} {payment_items} and this can end cleanly.
I will lower it this once: {payment_count} {payment_items}. Do not make me regret the mercy.
That is as far as I bend. {payment_count} {payment_items}, and the matter rests.
No. The amount stands. Do not spend trust you have not earned.
No bargain. Pay what was asked or choose another answer.
You opened the problem. You do not get to name its whole price.
Fine, here's {payment_count} {payment_items}
That's far too much
No way!
Threaten
That settles this for now.
Payment accepted. Next time, permission comes first.
That covers the damage. It does not erase the lesson.
You do not have {payment_count} {payment_items}. Then choose another answer.
That is not enough to pay what you offered. Try another answer.
Empty hands cannot settle this payment. Choose again.
Then you choose the harder memory.
Refusal is an answer. The village will remember it.
So be it. You leave this worse than you found it.
Then we are past words.
A threat answers the question clearly enough.
You chose force. The village heard you.
That is enough. Next time, ask before reaching.
Reduced or not, the payment is accepted. Do better next time.
That settles the bargain. Do not make us bargain over trust again.
